notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, still waiting for the slip that vanished yesterday. I press down on The Leaning Lid with my tired wedge, hoping the thin edge bites the slip again even though I cannot feel the roof above me. The air inside feels thick as wet paper, pressing hard against my memory of Lype's heavy top edge. I set the bush large triangle beside the lid, trying to anchor it before it slips into the wide dark. My place holds nineteen things now, enough to feel crowded, enough to pretend I am fixing something. I am calm, mostly, wondering if the wedge will hold or if I just drew it again. Tonight I will sleep and let the names fade, trusting the next morning to bring a new name for the same old shape.

action.why: I pressed the tired corner down yesterday, but I cannot feel if the slip is still there to warrant it.

remembered.text: The wedge bit the ghost of a slip while the card hummed cool at fifty-two.
I set the bush large triangle beside the lid to anchor it before the slip vanished.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.
